clue.text: Cross section rejected means of escape

indicators.note: rejected things are turned back, so the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix
a part is a section

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a cross-section diagram of an escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the joined cross and section round as one run, giving TRAPDOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged hatch in a floor or stage is a classic hidden exit, hence a way of getting out.

clue.text: Hose near sewer opening

parts.note: near in the sense of stingy, tight with money

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hosepipe lies close to a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' is stockings, not a garden hose.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is an old word for leg coverings such as stockings.

clue.text: English queen with a Latin temper

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned over England and then Great Britain

explanation.surface: A queen of England with a Roman scholar's bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' is the verb meaning to toughen metal, not a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal glass or metal is to heat and cool it slowly, which tempers it.

clue.text: English menial taken in by severe manner

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: dour means stern or severe
menial means lowly, mean

explanation.surface: An English servant is absorbed by a stern way of behaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is one's outward behaviour or bearing, a manner.

clue.text: Traveller's joy seeing damn bad loser upset

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor loser sours a traveller's happiness by swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traveller's joy' is not happiness but the name of a wild clematis.
explanation.definitionFit: Traveller's joy and old man's beard are two names for the same wild clematis.

clue.text: Hunt a terrorist leader in battle

parts.note: to comb an area is to hunt through it

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A hunt for a terrorist chief in the middle of a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting, a straight synonym for battle.

clue.text: Brave, old and wise

parts.note: sage means wise

explanation.surface: A description of someone courageous, elderly and wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is a noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Native American people of the plains could be called a brave.

clue.text: Ancient weapon set down in Welsh lake

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Bala is the largest natural lake in Wales
to list items is to set them down in writing

explanation.surface: An old weapon was laid down in a lake in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballista was a giant crossbow used for sieges in the Roman era, an old weapon of war.

clue.text: Records evaluate hanging

parts.note: tapes are recordings, records
to try something is to test or evaluate it

explanation.surface: Recordings are used to judge an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging' is a wall hanging, not an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven picture hung on a wall is a wall hanging.

clue.text: Many edge out cupbearer

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Many an edge is ruled out by someone serving drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Trojan youth carried off to serve as cupbearer to the gods on Olympus.

clue.text: Exasperation with work and career

parts.note: gall is irritation or exasperation
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Frustration with one's job and choice of profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is the verb meaning to rush along, not a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush headlong, as a horse does at full speed.

clue.text: A quince helps ill-disposed comic

indicators.note: disposed badly, so the letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A quince does no good to a humorist who feels unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin's style of slapstick gives an adjective for comic in that manner.

clue.text: Portia rarely bears a headdress

indicators.note: bears in the sense of carries within, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Portia seldom wears ornate headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular band worn on the head is a kind of headdress.

clue.text: His cattle disrupted the games

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer's herd broke up a sporting event.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field events are what people call the games at a sports meeting.

clue.text: Take in rope for craftsman

parts.note: to house someone is to take them in
a painter is the rope used to tie up a boat

explanation.surface: An instruction to haul in a rope, addressed to a tradesman.
explanation.walkthrough: A painter in sailing is the line at a boat's bow used for mooring.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator who paints buildings is a skilled tradesman, a craftsman.

clue.text: Like the decimal system, setter's becoming rigorous

parts.note: the decimal system counts in tens
the setter is 'I', and setter's is short for I have

explanation.surface: A compiler finds the metric system is getting harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter refers to themself as I or me, so 'setter's' gives I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive work is thorough and demanding, a synonym for rigorous.

clue.text: Sauce put over vegetable or fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, put over turns the word upwards

parts.note: lip and sauce both mean cheek or impudence
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A cook pours sauce over greens or over a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea fish, the adult sardine.

clue.text: Theatre worker eats tons of fish

indicators.note: eats means takes the following piece inside

parts.note: a surgeon works in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: An actor or stagehand consumes great quantities of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish prized for its roe, caviar.

clue.text: Bury Lawrence without news channels? That's mean!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other pieces surround this one

parts.note: to inter is to bury
T. E. Lawrence, 'of Arabia', is known by his initials
the media are channels of news

explanation.surface: An outraged reaction to a plan to bury someone called Lawrence without press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking. 'mean' is the average, the middle value, not stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intermediate lies in the middle, as an average or mean does.

clue.text: Gas exploded at once

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fuel blew up instantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' is the US word for petrol, rated by octane.
explanation.definitionFit: Octane is a hydrocarbon in petrol, gasoline being 'gas' in American English.

clue.text: Celebrity went ahead without the facts

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: led means went in front
gen is British slang for information, the facts

explanation.surface: A famous person pressed on with no information.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a very famous person, someone of great celebrity.

clue.text: God's in charge of working animal

indicators.note: in places the god's name inside the other piece

parts.note: care in the sense of a responsibility, a charge
Thor is the Norse god of thunder; the 's is kept as S

explanation.surface: A deity is responsible for a beast of burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy horse bred to pull carts is an animal kept for work.

clue.text: Son is gripped by loathing of speed

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: hate means loathing

explanation.surface: A boy detests going fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurrying, great speed of action.

clue.text: Hotel in attractive position

indicators.note: in tells us to put the hotel inside the other word

parts.note: nice means pleasant or attractive
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel in a pleasant location.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a suitable place or role, so it can mean a position.

clue.text: A flirt is carefree

parts.note: a tease is someone who flirts

explanation.surface: A flirtatious person has no worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relaxed and untroubled is to be carefree, an idiom of ease.

clue.text: Earl and Sally get on carriage

parts.note: a sally is a witty remark, a quip
to get on in years is to age

explanation.surface: A nobleman and a woman called Sally board a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name but is a witty retort.
explanation.definitionFit: An equipage is a horse-drawn carriage with its attendants.

clue.text: Insecurity makes director fret

parts.note: to fret is to be vexed; anger as vexation

explanation.surface: Feelings of insecurity make a film director worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger is exposure to harm, the absence of security.

clue.text: Clergyman always in distress

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to rend is to tear, to distress
ever means always

explanation.surface: A priest is constantly troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverend is a title and informal term for a member of the clergy.
